Field notes on soil drainage

Last updated March 2026 · Back to the index

Heavy clay holds water near the surface long after rain. The fastest way to check your soil is the jar test: fill a mason jar a third full with soil, top it with water, shake hard, and leave it overnight.

What the layers mean

Sand settles first, then silt, then clay. The band widths give you rough percentages. Anything over forty percent clay drains slowly and benefits from raised beds.

LayerSettles inFeel
Sand1 minuteGritty
Silt2 hoursFloury
ClayOvernightSticky

Fixing a waterlogged bed

Compost is the honest answer. Gypsum helps sodic soils only, despite what the bag promises. A two-inch layer worked into the top eight inches each fall will change the structure within three seasons.

Drainage problems are structure problems. Structure comes from organic matter and time.
